candidates.name: beat_this (CPJKU) 1.1.0
candidates.last_release: 1.1.0 on 2026-04-14 (first PyPI release; 1.0 was 2024-10-18). Changelog adds infer_beat_numbers(), saving raw logits from the CLI, support for non-CUDA accelerators, and weights_only checkpoint loading.
candidates.license: MIT for both the code and the published weights. The README warns that some training data has its own licences.
candidates.provides: Beat and downbeat times, framewise beat/downbeat logits at 50 fps (Audio2Frames), and beat-in-bar numbers (infer_beat_numbers, which handles pickup bars). Default postprocessing is 'minimal': max-pool peak picking with logit > 0. An optional DBN mode uses madmom DBNDownBeatTrackingProcessor with beats_per_bar [3,4] and 55-215 BPM.
candidates.windows_install: wheels-on-pypi. Ships a py3-none-any wheel and resolves on Windows py3.12 with uv (torch 2.15.0 CPU wheel, torchaudio 2.11.1, einops, rotary-embedding-torch 0.9.2, soxr). The --dbn flag needs madmom, which is a problem on Windows (see madmom).
candidates.amd_gpu: Pure PyTorch, so it runs on any torch device (1.1.0 added non-CUDA accelerators). It could use AMD's PyTorch-on-Windows ROCm build, but CPU is enough. MIT ONNX ports also exist (musetric/beat-this-onnx, 2026-10) for an onnxruntime / DirectML path without torch.
candidates.speed_estimate: Estimate, not measured: about 3-10 s on CPU for a 4-minute song with final0 (78 MB). small0 (8 MB) takes about 1-2 s. Inference runs in 1500-frame (30 s) chunks.
candidates.quality_notes: State of the art at ISMIR 2024 without a DBN. Because it does not lock to one tempo, it follows tempo changes and expressive timing better than DBN pipelines. Beat times sit on a 20 ms grid, so they need sub-frame refinement for 60 fps cuts. Downbeats are weaker in non-4/4 and sparse sections, and it can emit no beats or phantom beats in ambient passages.
candidates.reason: The best accuracy per dependency: MIT code and weights, a pure-Python wheel, actively maintained in 2026, gives logits for confidence and handles tempo changes. It is the primary source for beats and downbeats.

candidates.name: all-in-one-infer 3.1.0 (openmirlab fork of allin1)
candidates.url: https://github.com/openmirlab/all-in-one-infer (PyPI all-in-one-infer 3.1.0 is a historical snapshot; new versions ship from git only)
candidates.last_release: PyPI 3.1.0 on 2026-07-12. Git main had commits up to 2026-10-08.
candidates.license: MIT for the code. The original allin1 weights (taejunkim/allinone on Hugging Face) are MIT.
candidates.provides: Functional segments with labels from the Harmonix vocabulary: start, end, intro, outro, break, bridge, inst, solo, verse, chorus. Also BPM, beats, downbeats and beat_positions. Optional 100 fps activations: beat, downbeat, segment-boundary sigmoids and a 10-class label softmax. Optional embeddings [4 stems, T, 24]. Accepts precomputed bass/drums/other/vocals stems (stems_input, PrecomputedStemProvider, skip_separation). Includes sonify() for click and boundary-cue review audio.
candidates.windows_install: wheels-on-pypi. 3.1.0 is py3-none-any. With beat-this and librosa 1.0.0 it resolves cleanly on Windows py3.12 into a 66-package lock: torch 2.15.0, demucs-infer 4.4.0, madmom-infer 0.2.0, julius 0.2.8 wheels, and antlr4-python3-runtime 4.9.3, which is a pure-Python sdist. The README lists Linux, macOS and Windows and says CI runs Python 3.9-3.12 on CPU. Pure-PyTorch neighborhood attention replaces NATTEN, and madmom-infer (numpy) replaces Cython madmom.
candidates.amd_gpu: Optional via PyTorch ROCm on Windows. Device accepts 'cpu', 'cuda' and 'auto', and rejects 'mps'. Most of the cost is HTDemucs separation, which can be shared with the stems/instruments track.
candidates.speed_estimate: Estimate: with precomputed stems, about 20-50 s on CPU for harmonix-all (8 folds, pure-PyTorch neighborhood attention, plus madmom-infer DBN decoding). A single fold (harmonix-fold0) is about 5-15 s. If it runs HTDemucs itself, add about 45-90 s on CPU. Reference point: an RTX 4090 did 10 songs (33 minutes of audio) in 73 s, with under 0.5 s of model forward per song.
candidates.quality_notes: The strongest open model for functional labels plus a metrical grid that runs on Windows CPU. Trained on Harmonix (pop/EDM, mostly 4/4). It has no pre-chorus, drop or build-up labels, so EDM roles must come from custom code. BPM is an integer. Label probabilities give a usable confidence.
candidates.reason: The only Windows-native way to run the All-In-One models: unchanged weights, no NATTEN or Cython build. It supplies structure labels and a second, independent beat/downbeat/BPM estimate for cross-checking. It reuses the same HTDemucs stems as other tracks. Pin a git SHA, with PyPI 3.1.0 as a fallback.

candidates.name: allin1 1.1.0 (original, mir-aidj/all-in-one)
candidates.provides: Same outputs as all-in-one-infer.

candidates.speed_estimate: n/a

output_fields.name: tempo
output_fields.description: Global tempo after arbitration, with alternatives and the evidence behind them. 'feel' flags half-time or double-time grooves, for example a 140 BPM track whose kick pattern implies 70.
output_fields.representation: object {bpm, confidence 0-1, feel: normal|half_time|double_time, candidates:[{bpm, score, relation:'x1|x2|x0.5|x1.5|x0.667|x1.333|x0.75'}], estimates:{beat_this_ibi, allin1, librosa_or_acf}, agreement:'agree|octave|ternary|4:3|disagree', is_variable bool}
output_fields.source: beat_this IBI median, all-in-one-infer bpm, librosa feature.tempo / ported audio.js ACF; custom arbitration

output_fields.name: tempo_curve
output_fields.description: Local tempo over time, plus piecewise-constant tempo segments for agents that want stable regions.
output_fields.representation: curve sampled at 2 Hz {t0, hz, bpm[], conf[]} plus segment list tempo_segments:[{start, end, bpm, stable bool}]
output_fields.source: smoothed beat_this inter-beat intervals; confidence from librosa tempogram/PLP peak clarity; change-point detection (custom)

output_fields.name: beats
output_fields.description: Every beat, for cutting and pulsing. Beats inferred in pulse-less regions are flagged so agents do not cut on phantom beats.
output_fields.representation: event list [{t (s, 3 decimals), i, bar, pos (1..N), strength (beat_this peak prob 0-1), accent (kick/onset strength at beat 0-1), conf, inferred bool}] plus grid_beats[] (regularised times) and pulse_regions:[{start, end, has_pulse}]
output_fields.source: beat_this 1.1.0 final0 + infer_beat_numbers; refinement and accent from custom kick envelope / librosa onsets

output_fields.name: bars
output_fields.description: Downbeats and bars, for scene switches on the '1'. Each bar records its length in beats, which shows odd bars.
output_fields.representation: event list [{t, bar, beats_in_bar, dur, conf, section_id, phrase_id}]
output_fields.source: beat_this downbeats, cross-checked against allin1 downbeats (agreement F-measure); madmom-infer DBN fallback

output_fields.name: meter
output_fields.description: Time signature and any changes in it.
output_fields.representation: object {time_signature:'4/4', beats_per_bar, confidence, changes:[{t, beats_per_bar}], irregular_bars:[bar indices]}
output_fields.source: mode of beats per downbeat interval + librosa metrogram; custom

output_fields.name: phrases
output_fields.description: Hypermetric phrases of 4, 8 or 16 bars aligned to section starts. These are the natural units for longer shots and transitions.
output_fields.representation: segment list [{id, start, end, start_bar, n_bars, section_id}]
output_fields.source: custom: choose the phrase length that maximises alignment of novelty and boundary peaks with phrase starts

output_fields.name: onsets
output_fields.description: Per-band transient events using the viz band rule, from the mix and from the drums stem (kick, snare and hat proxies), plus onset density.
output_fields.representation: per-band event lists {bass|mid|high|kick|snare|hat: [{t, strength 0-1}]}; onset_density curve at 10 Hz; onset envelopes as float16 sidecar at 100 Hz
output_fields.source: librosa onset_strength_multi / onset_detect(backtrack) + ported audio.js kick envelope (8 ms / 90 ms envelopes, typical-attack reference, 4 dB re-arm, -46 dBFS gate)

output_fields.name: sections
output_fields.description: Functional song sections with confidence and repetition info, snapped to downbeats. Covers loud and quiet parts through per-section energy and rank.
output_fields.representation: segment list [{id, start, end, start_bar, n_bars, label (intro|verse|pre-chorus|chorus|bridge|inst|solo|break|outro), label_conf, label_probs{}, role (EDM layer: build|drop|breakdown|null), repeat_group 'A'..., occurrence n, similarity_to_group 0-1, boundary_conf, energy_db, bass_db, energy_rank, delta_db_from_prev, is_peak bool}]
output_fields.source: all-in-one-infer harmonix-all (labels, softmax, boundary activation) or optional SongFormer; custom snapping, repetition grouping and energy features

output_fields.name: repetition
output_fields.description: Which sections repeat, so agents can reuse a visual motif for each repeat of a section.
output_fields.representation: object {groups:{A:{label, sections:[ids], mean_similarity}}, segment_similarity: N x N matrix (small)}
output_fields.source: custom cosine similarity on segment-mean beat-synchronous chroma, MFCC and allin1 embeddings (librosa recurrence as a cross-check)

output_fields.name: dynamics_events
output_fields.description: Drops, build-ups, breakdowns and silences or gaps, used to anticipate impacts. A build carries a rising tension ramp and points at its target drop.
output_fields.representation: event and segment list [{type:'drop', t (snapped to downbeat), bar, bass_jump_db, energy_jump_db, conf, build_id}], [{type:'build', start, end, n_bars, target_t, cues:['bass_cut','riser','snare_roll','filter_sweep','pre_drop_gap'], conf}], [{type:'breakdown', start, end}], [{type:'gap', start, end, depth_db}]; plus a tension curve at 10 Hz (0-1)
output_fields.source: custom bar-level detectors on mix and stems (RMS/bass dB, kick count, onset density, spectral centroid/high-band slope, vocal-stem activity)

output_fields.name: cues
output_fields.description: One merged, time-sorted cue sheet that agents filter by priority to set cut density, with lead-in times for anticipation.
output_fields.representation: event list [{t, kind: section|drop|build_start|phrase|downbeat|beat|kick|snare|gap, priority 0 (section/drop) ... 4 (onset), strength, ref_id, lead_in_s (time since previous cue of priority <= this one), next_major_in_s}]
output_fields.source: custom merge of the fields above

output_fields.name: rhythm_qa
output_fields.description: Confidence and agreement metrics and warning flags, so agents know when to fall back to free-running animation.
output_fields.representation: object {beat_agreement_f (beat_this vs allin1, ±70 ms), downbeat_agreement_f, tempo_ratio, flags:['tempo_ambiguous','variable_tempo','odd_meter','pulse_gaps','structure_low_conf','decode_warnings'], model_versions, model_sha256}
output_fields.source: custom (mir_eval-style F-measure) + provenance

output_fields.name: review_exports
output_fields.description: Files a person can use to view or listen to the beats, bars, sections and loud/quiet events without writing code. This meets the requirement that beats and loud/quiet parts can be viewed.
output_fields.representation: files: beats.txt, bars.txt, sections.txt and dynamics.txt as Audacity label tracks (start\tend\tlabel), click_preview.flac (clicks on beats and accented downbeats, boundary cues), and a viewer-ready JSON (same schema) for the harness timeline viewer
output_fields.source: custom writers + allin1_infer.sonify or own click synthesis

custom_code_needed: Canonical decode wrapper around ffmpeg 9.0.2 (float32 WAV at 44.1 kHz, plus mono and 22.05/24 kHz copies) that records decoder warnings. Verified: Versatile.flac has a corrupt frame that libsndfile/soundfile cannot read but ffmpeg conceals.

Tempo arbitration: compare the beat_this IBI median, allin1 BPM and librosa (or the ported audio.js ACF with 2x/4x harmonic support). Classify ratios as 1, 2, 1/2, 3/2, 2/3, 4/3 or 3/4, apply a log-normal prior near 120 BPM, and compute confidence from agreement, mean beat probability, IBI variation and tempogram peak ratio. The numpy probe on MEGAFAUNA.flac found 105 vs 140 BPM, a 4:3 metrical ambiguity rather than an octave; Versatile.flac was a steady 130 BPM with 65 and 87 as weaker candidates.

Beat refinement: parabolic sub-frame interpolation of beat_this logits (50 fps is a 20 ms grid, coarser than a 16.7 ms video frame at 60 fps), snapping to the nearest transient within ±25 ms, and a regularised grid from robust piecewise-linear fits inside stable tempo segments.
Meter inference from downbeat spacing plus the librosa metrogram, detection of irregular bars and pickups, and a madmom-infer DBN fallback with beats_per_bar (3,4,6) when downbeats are inconsistent.
Phrase (hypermeter) detection: choose a 4, 8 or 16-bar grouping offset that best aligns novelty and boundary peaks with phrase starts.

Section post-processing: snap boundaries to the nearest downbeat (within 1 beat), merge segments shorter than 2 bars, and number occurrences. Repetition grouping uses segment-mean beat-synchronous chroma, MFCC and allin1 24-dim stem embeddings with cosine similarity and agglomerative clustering (A/B/C plus similarity).

Offline port of the viz/js/audio.js kick envelope (35-100 Hz band power in dB, gap between 8 ms and 90 ms envelopes, typical-attack reference, re-arm after a 4 dB dip, -46 dBFS gate) and of the per-band spectral-flux onsets using the band rule (32-150 / 150-2200 / 2200-16k Hz, 2.6 dB/oct tilt for display curves). Run it non-causally on the mix and on the drums stem so offline kick strengths match the live visualiser.

Bar-level dynamics features (RMS dB, bass dB, kick count, onset density, spectral centroid / high-band slope, vocal-stem RMS) and detectors. Drop: a bass jump of at least 9 dB and an energy jump of at least 3 dB at a downbeat, into a top-30% energy section. Build: the up to 16 bars before a drop or chorus with rising density or centroid and/or a bass cut, plus snare-roll doubling. Breakdown: no kicks for 2 or more bars and energy below the median minus 6 dB. Gap: under -50 dBFS for at least 150 ms. Also a 0-1 tension curve. The probe showed clear bass-cut builds in Versatile (around 44-52 s and 156-164 s; drops around 52 s and 164 s) and a quiet break followed by a gap around 92 s in MEGAFAUNA.
Confidence and QA: beat and downbeat F-measure between beat_this and allin1 (±70 ms), pulse-region detection to suppress phantom beats, and model version / SHA-256 provenance.
Cue-sheet merger with priority levels and anticipation fields (lead_in_s, next_major_in_s, a build's target_t).
Review exporters: Audacity label tracks, a click/boundary sonified preview, and JSON for the harness's timeline viewer.

Model cache and offline mode: pre-fetch beat_this final0 (JKU cloud; the URL has already changed once, per the 1.1.0 changelog), allin1 harmonix-fold0..7 (Hugging Face) and htdemucs weights into a harness-owned cache with SHA-256 checks.
risks: The openmirlab packages (all-in-one-infer, madmom-infer, demucs-infer) are 2026 reimplementations from one organisation and are no longer published to PyPI. Mitigate by pinning git SHAs, caching built wheels, and keeping PyPI 3.1.0 / 0.2.0 / 4.4.0 as the fallback.
Harmonix label vocabulary: no pre-chorus, drop or build-up, and a pop/EDM 4/4 bias. EDM roles must come from custom detectors, and labels on unusual forms may be wrong (chorus vs inst).
Metrical ambiguity is not only octave errors. The MEGAFAUNA probe gives 105 vs 140 BPM (4:3). Arbitration must handle 4:3 and 3:2, and report feel and alternatives instead of a single number.

Decode robustness: Versatile.flac contains a corrupt frame. soundfile and torchaudio paths can crash or mis-align, so always decode with ffmpeg first. Different MP3 decoders shift audio by 20-40 ms (noted in the all-in-one-infer README).
Time resolution: beat_this is at 50 fps (20 ms) and allin1 at 100 fps, while video frames at 60 fps are 16.7 ms. Without refinement, cuts can land a frame late.

Licensing: madmom model weights used by madmom-infer's RNN processors are CC BY-NC-SA, and MuQ (used by SongFormer) is CC BY-NC. Fine for personal use; a problem for commercial output. beat_this and allin1 weights are MIT.

torch version drift: PyPI torch 2.15 CPU works. AMD's Windows ROCm build is torch 2.9, which conflicts with torchaudio 2.11.1 (requires torch>=2.11), so a GPU env needs AMD's torchaudio and a separate lock. Newer torchaudio.load depends on torchcodec; pass arrays to beat_this (Audio2Frames) instead of file paths.
First-run cost: numba JIT for librosa (10-30 s, then cached) and about 1 GB of model downloads (htdemucs plus 8 allin1 folds plus beat_this). Third-party download hosts can change URLs.
SongFormer (optional) is fragile: transformers==4.51.1 pin, msaf pulling enum34 (breaks the stdlib enum on 3.12), Linux/CUDA-only testing, about 3 GB of weights, and slow CPU inference.
madmom-prebuilt has an unknown publisher (supply-chain risk). Avoid it unless compiled madmom is truly needed.
Speed figures for the torch models are estimates, because torch was not installed in this research. Benchmark beat_this and all-in-one-infer on both test songs before fixing the 5-minute budget.
No-pulse sections (ambient intros, rubato) can produce phantom or missing beats. Without pulse_regions and conf, agents would cut on noise.

recommended_stack:
Pinned packages: numpy==2.5.*, scipy==1.18.*, librosa==1.0.*, pyloudnorm==0.2.0, soundfile==0.14.*, soxr==1.1.*, onnxruntime==1.31.* (S-KEY). Add lv-chordia==1.1.0 + torch==2.15.* (PyPI CPU wheel) only if the harness carries torch anyway. External: ffmpeg 9.0.2. uv pip compile confirms all of these resolve for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc / py3.12 with --only-binary :all:.

1. DECODE: ffmpeg -v warning -i <song> -map 0:a:0 -vn -c:a pcm_f32le <work>/audio.wav at native sample rate and channels. Never read the original with libsndfile. Record ffmpeg warnings, sr, channels, duration and the sha256 of the PCM in the manifest. t=0 is the first decoded sample.

2. GRID: every curve sits on one fixed 100 Hz grid. Frame i is centred at t=i/100 s (sample round(i*sr/100)). STFT of mid (L+R)/2 and side (L-R)/2: N=2048 for sr up to 50 kHz (4096 for 88.2/96 kHz), Blackman window, |X|/N scaling (AnalyserNode-compatible dB), chunked numpy.fft.rfft, float32.

3. SPECTRUM: port of audio.js _computeBandMap/update. 128 log bands from 32 Hz to 16 kHz with identical edges. Each band is the mean of per-bin dB, with linear interpolation for bands narrower than one bin. Add 2.6 dB/oct tilt, map (dB+88)/70, apply ONE per-song gain (0.95 / p99.5 of the per-frame max band) instead of AGC, then soft knee v/(1+0.18v). Store as u8.

4. BANDS: power-domain dB (10log10 of summed bin power) for the viz bands (bass 32-150, mid 150-2200, high 2200-16k), for 7 finer bands (sub 20-60, bass 60-150, lowmid 150-500, mid 500-2k, highmid 2-4k, presence 4-6k, air 6-16k) and for kick 35-100. Each gets a 0..1 per-song copy (p2 to p99.5 of its own dB, with lo/hi stored). Also store the viz-compatible 0..1 bass/mid/high (mean of the normalised log bands).

5. HIT ENVELOPES: a straight port of _hitEnvelope at dt=10 ms for kick (eKick from 35-100 Hz power, gate -46 dBFS), mid and high. Offline upgrades:
   (a) typical-attack reference = centred ±8 s median of attack peaks, so there is no warm-up;
   (b) the gate becomes relative: max(-46, kick-band p95 - 30 dB);
   (c) event time is refined to the steepest rise of a 2.5 ms-hop zero-phase (sosfiltfilt) 35-100 Hz envelope;
   (d) emit both raw (no release) and released (0.18 s) curves, plus an event list.
   Run the loop in plain Python (0.3 s) or numba.

6. ONSETS: per-band positive spectral flux on the normalised log bands (low 32-260, mid 300-2200, high 2500-14k). Threshold = centred moving mean over ±0.25 s × 1.55 (low) / 1.7 (mid, high) + 0.012. Keep local maxima with min gap 0.16 / 0.12 / 0.08 s. Strength uses the viz formula.

7. LOUDNESS: pyloudnorm K-weighting filters (meter._filters) per channel, then cumulative sums, giving lufs_m (0.4 s) and lufs_s (3 s) CENTRED at 100 Hz. Spec meters trail, so a spec value equals ours at t-0.2 s or t-1.5 s; document this. Integrated loudness and LRA come from pyloudnorm.Meter. True peak and the cross-check come from ffmpeg -af ebur128=peak=true (parse the summary; warn if the I difference exceeds 0.5 LU). Also rms_db and peak_db per frame, crest factor and PLR.

8. TIMBRE/STEREO: centroid, rolloff85, flatness, bandwidth (32 Hz-16 kHz), ZCR, total flux. Stereo width = side/(mid+side) energy, Pearson L/R correlation, balance dB, and per-band width from the side STFT.

9. HARMONY: librosa resample to 22050 (soxr_hq), then librosa.effects.harmonic(margin=2), then chroma_cqt(36 bpo, 6 octaves from C1, hop 512). Interpolate chroma12 onto the 100 Hz grid and keep the H/P energy ratio as a curve.

10. KEY: S-KEY ONNX on the whole song (global) and on 30 s windows with a 10 s hop. Smooth with a sticky Viterbi into key segments. The in-house estimator runs alongside (Krumhansl + Temperley + EDMA profiles on bass-weighted chroma plus a chord-root histogram from step 11). Report both and flag disagreement or a relative major/minor tie.

11. CHORDS: lv-chordia chord_recognition(local_path, 'submission') gives segments, simplified to maj/min/7 and root pitch class. Fallback: 25-class template matching plus librosa.sequence.viterbi(transition_loop(25, 0.97)). Snap boundaries to the nearest beat within 80 ms once the beats track has run.

12. DYNAMICS SEGMENTATION: a 10 Hz feature matrix (lufs_m, viz bass/mid/high dB, kick-event rate, log centroid, width, onset density), median-smoothed and z-scored, then Foote checkerboard novelty (±8 s, or ±4 bars once the beat grid exists). Peaks become boundaries, snapped to downbeats. Each segment gets a level class from LU relative to integrated (silence / quiet <-8 / soft <-4 / medium / loud >-1.5 / peak) and tags (intro, outro, build-up, drop, breakdown, fade-in, fade-out). Also detect silences (rms < -60 dBFS for 0.4 s or more), impact events (lufs_m +6 LU within 200 ms after 1 s or more quieter, or bass +6 dB) and stop/cut events.

13. INTENSITY: a 0..1 composite of short-term LU relative to integrated (-20..+3 mapped to 0..1, weight 0.5), bass dB normalised (0.25), onset density (0.15) and centroid normalised (0.10), smoothed over 0.5 s.

14. WRITE:
   - analysis.json: manifest (format version, audio info, fps=100, frames, and a curve registry with name, unit, range, norm lo/hi, resample agg rule mean|max|interp, byte offset), scalars, events, segments, key, chords.
   - curves_100hz.f32: column-major little-endian float32, one contiguous block per curve, so in JS new Float32Array(buf, off, frames).
   - spectrum128_100hz.u8: row-major [frame][128], uploadable directly as an R8 texture.
   - digest.json and digest.md at 1 Hz or per bar, for LLM agents.
   - Optional: curves_<fps>.csv per requested fps, and Parquet.
   Ship resample_to_fps(curve, fps, agg) in Python and as a JS snippet: max-pool for hit envelopes and flux, mean for levels and spectra, interp for slow curves. Events stay as float seconds.

15. VIEWER (covers the user's 'viewing loud/quiet parts' requirement): a static HTML page that reads analysis.json and the .f32/.u8 files. Lanes: waveform/loudness with loud/quiet/build/drop sections shaded, spectrogram, bass/mid/high, kick ticks, chord and key lane.

Measured total for steps 1-9, 11 (fallback) and 12-14 on this PC: 14.7 s (Versatile, 228 s, warm) and 23.3 s (MEGAFAUNA, 217 s, first-run numba JIT). Estimated with lv-chordia and S-KEY: 40-90 s CPU for a 4-min song, well under the 5-min budget. No GPU needed for this track.

custom_code_needed: Web-Audio-compatible offline STFT (Blackman, |X|/N, centred frames on a fixed 100 Hz grid, chunked rfft of mid and side), so viz constants (-88/-18 dB, -46 dBFS gate, 2.6 dB/oct tilt) carry over unchanged.

Port of audio.js _computeBandMap + band loop: 128 log bands with identical edges, mean-of-dB, sub-bin interpolation, tilt, soft knee. Per-song gain (p99.5) replaces the 6 s-peak / 2 s AGC. Optional centred rolling-percentile 'local' normalisation reproduces the AGC look without lag.

Port of _hitEnvelope (kick/mid/high) with offline changes: centred ±8 s median reference (no warm-up), relative kick gate max(-46, kick-band p95 - 30 dB), raw and released outputs, re-arm logic kept, event extraction, and onset-time refinement from a 2.5 ms zero-phase 35-100 Hz envelope (the fast-minus-slow gap peaks 10-30 ms after the true onset).
Port of _flux/_threshold per band with a centred (non-causal) adaptive threshold and look-ahead local-max picking.

Momentary and short-term LUFS curves at 100 Hz from pyloudnorm K-weighting via cumulative sums (centred), plus a parser for the ffmpeg ebur128 summary (I, LRA, true peak) that cross-checks and warns on mismatch.
Stereo width / correlation / balance per frame and per band.

Dynamics segmentation: Foote novelty on a 10 Hz multi-feature matrix, downbeat snapping, level classes relative to integrated LUFS, rule tags (intro, outro, build-up, drop, breakdown, fade, silence), impact and stop events. Thresholds need tuning on more songs (in the prototype an outro was tagged 'breakdown').
Intensity composite curve.

Key: profile ensemble (Krumhansl, Temperley, EDMA) on bass-weighted chroma + chord-root histogram + sticky Viterbi for modulations. An S-KEY ONNX wrapper (22.05 kHz mono, peak-normalised, 30 s windows), and a one-off export script from the official deezer/skey checkpoint with sha256 pinning.
Chord fallback (25-class templates + librosa Viterbi), a Harte/JAMS label simplifier for lv-chordia output, and beat-snapping of chord and section boundaries.

resample_to_fps(curve, fps, agg) in Python and JS: max-pool for hit envelopes and flux so no hit falls between video frames, mean for levels and spectra, interp for slow curves. Plus frame-index helpers for events.
Manifest writer: curve registry with unit, norm lo/hi, agg rule and byte offsets, column-major float32 LE curves file, row-major u8 spectrum file.
Digest generator (per bar / 1 Hz table + prose) so LLM agents get the gist without reading 24,000-row curves (CSV at 100 Hz is about 6-7 MB, JSON about 6.8 MB).

Static HTML viewer with lanes (loudness with loud/quiet/build/drop shading, spectrogram, bands, kick ticks, chords, key). It answers the user's 'viewing loud/quiet parts' requirement without matplotlib.
risks: Decoding: soundfile/libsndfile 0.14.0 failed on Versatile.flac with 'flac decoder lost sync', while ffmpeg decoded it after one invalid-frame warning. Both FLACs also carry an MJPEG cover-art stream. Decode only via ffmpeg -map 0:a:0 -vn and record the warnings.

Licences: S-KEY weights are non-commercial research only per Deezer's README, and the HF ONNX card's 'MIT' contradicts that. madmom models are CC BY-NC-SA. essentia is AGPL. Only lv-chordia (MIT) and the in-house estimator are commercially clean.

PyPI name collision: 'skey' on PyPI is an unrelated 'SecureKey test' package. Never pip install skey. The real S-KEY is GitHub-only (poetry, pins torch~2.7 / numpy~2.2, which conflicts with a current stack).

lv-chordia drags in torch (127 MB CPU wheel, several hundred MB installed). It loads pickled checkpoints, has a URL auto-download feature (pass local paths only), and is maintained by a third-party repackager. Its CPU speed was not verified (estimate 15-60 s).
madmom-prebuilt is an unofficial single-maintainer rebuild. It resolves with numpy 2.5.4, but numpy-2 runtime behaviour was not verified.

Template-based key is weak. With 8 s windows it changed key 9 times on MEGAFAUNA, and relative major/minor ties are common (D minor 0.67 vs D major 0.60). Needs longer windows, stickier transitions and a learned model.

Heavily limited masters (Versatile I = -6.0 LUFS, true peak +4.1 dBTP; MEGAFAUNA +0.3 dBTP) give flat LUFS in loud sections, so loud/quiet and drop detection must also use bass dB, kick density and spectral features. An absolute -46 dBFS kick gate also behaves differently across masters (make it relative).

Timing conventions: our windows are centred, but spec meters trail (momentary +0.2 s, short-term +1.5 s). MP3/AAC decoder priming can shift t=0 by tens of ms. The video must use the same decoded audio, or the offset must be recorded.

Section labelling heuristics are unvalidated (no ground truth). In the prototype the drops (Versatile 47.5 s and 171.9 s, MEGAFAUNA 146.3 s) were plausible, but an outro was tagged as a breakdown. Tuning on more songs and beat snapping are needed.
librosa 1.0 is three months old and expired 0.x deprecations: pin 1.0.x. The first run pays about 8 s of numba JIT.
Size and format: float curves barely compress (gzip -10%). zstd Parquet was larger than raw f32. CSV/JSON at 100 Hz (about 6-7 MB) is too big for agent context windows, so a digest is mandatory.

GPU: not needed for this track. onnxruntime-directml (1.24.4, 2026-03) is DirectML maintenance-era, torch-directml is stale (2024-09), and ROCm-on-Windows PyTorch for RDNA4 is still a preview (ROCm 7.2.x, Python 3.12).

Which video fps should the harness pre-render CSV/resampled curves for (24/30/60), or should it only ship the resample helper?
Pipeline order: section and chord boundaries should snap to the beats track's downbeats, so the beats track must run first.
Validate S-KEY ONNX locally (export from the official checkpoint vs pinned HF revision) and measure lv-chordia CPU time once torch is allowed.

NC licences apply.
- GPU profile: unblend ONNX graphs on DmlExecutionProvider with our own STFT/overlap-add host (verified 0.2 s per 7.8 s segment on the RX 9070).
- Pin every HF download by revision and SHA-256.

2) SAVE STEMS for video agents: yes. 16-bit 44.1 kHz stereo FLAC: 63 MB for 6 stems of 3:37, versus 220 MB as WAV. Also write instrumental.flac (mix minus vocals) and a stems manifest (model, licence, loudness, active ratio). A visual driven only by the vocal or bass stem is a key use case. Offer `--stem-format wav` for tools that cannot read FLAC.

3) STEM ACTIVITY (custom, 0.6 s): RMS dBFS at 50 Hz per stem, plus level relative to the mix. Active means above -45 dBFS and within -18 dB of the mix, with 300 ms on and 500 ms off hysteresis. Inactive stems skip the steps below and their notes are masked.

4) NOTES: basic-pitch ONNX (nmp.onnx) on bass, piano, guitar and other, called with arrays and not file paths.
- Bass preset: 30-400 Hz, minimum_note_length 80 ms.
- Others: onset 0.5 / frame 0.3 / minimum 127 ms, melodia on.
- Drop notes outside active segments. Write <stem>.mid and JSON events.
- About 1.5-2.2 s per stem.

5) VOCALS: swift-f0 on the vocal stem (mono, 16 kHz, fmin 65, fmax 1400).
- Contour: frames with confidence ≥ 0.5.
- Range statistics: confidence ≥ 0.8, vocal stem active, octave-jump cleanup with a median filter.
- Notes from segment_notes(pitch_hold_ms=80).
- If fewer than about 8 voiced seconds, set vocals.present=false and range=null. Both test songs are effectively instrumental (vocal stem 50-62 dB below the mix, 0-5% voiced).
- Fall back to RMVPE when the mean confidence is low or octave flips exceed about 5%.
- 0.4 s.

6) INSTRUMENTS: CED-base ONNX on CPU, 4 s windows with 1 s hop, on the mix and on the other, guitar and piano stems (about 5 s per pass).
- Map the 527 AudioSet classes to a curated instrument vocabulary.
- Fuse with stem activity: an instrument is reported only when the tagger and the matching stem agree, otherwise it is labelled 'guitar-like' or 'lead'.
- Singing, speech and rap probabilities on the vocal stem give the vocal style.
- Optional CLAP zero-shot for synth and electronic labels.

7) DRUMS: custom classifier on the drum stem, ported from audio.js.
- Kick: 35-100 Hz power in dB, fast 8 ms / slow 90 ms envelopes, typical-attack reference, 4 dB re-arm, -46 dBFS gate.
- Snare: 150-350 Hz body plus 1.5-6 kHz noise flux.
- Hat/cymbal: 7-16 kHz flux, split by decay length.
- Tom: 80-250 Hz pitched with longer decay.
- Outputs: events plus 100 Hz envelopes.
- Optional ADTOF-pytorch or DrumSep in the quality profile.

8) VIEWING (per the user's request): per-stem .mid files that open in any DAW, and JSON per field. Also an HTML report section with a piano roll per stem, instrument lanes over time, the vocal contour with a keyboard range bar marking lowest, highest and tessitura, and a drum-hit raster.

custom_code_needed: ffmpeg decode wrapper: canonical 44.1 kHz stereo float32, first audio stream only (cover art dropped), tolerant of corrupt FLAC frames, with loudness normalisation recorded but not applied. Every downstream tool reads this WAV or arrays, never the original file.

Optional ONNX host for the unblend separation graphs, to get DirectML on the RX 9070: centred normalised STFT (n_fft 4096, reflect pad 1536, drop top bin, trim 2 frames to get 336 frames), mean/std normalisation, triangular-window overlap-add at a 0.75*L hop, and iSTFT. About 150 lines, following unblend's onnx.md.
Stem activity: RMS dBFS at 50 Hz, level relative to the mix, active segments with hysteresis, and a 'stem present' decision.

Drum-hit classifier on the drum stem, ported from viz/js/audio.js: kick from 35-100 Hz band power in dB (8 ms / 90 ms envelopes, typical-attack reference, 4 dB re-arm, -46 dBFS gate). Snare, hat/cymbal and tom detectors added via band-limited spectral flux and decay length. Outputs events plus 100 Hz envelopes.
Per-stem spectral-flux onsets (audio.js thresholds: mult 1.55-1.7, refractory 80-160 ms).

Vocal presence and range statistics: confidence and activity gating, octave-error cleanup (median filter, ±12-semitone jump repair), p2/p98 lowest/highest, p10/p90 tessitura, phrase segmentation, voice-type mapping table, and an RMVPE-fallback trigger.
basic-pitch wrapper: pass numpy arrays instead of paths (its librosa.load path would hit libsndfile), per-stem frequency and threshold presets, masking by stem activity, MIDI and JSON export.

AudioSet → curated instrument vocabulary map (about 25 labels), fusion with stem activity (for example htdemucs_6s 'guitar' active but the tagger says Synthesizer becomes 'synth lead'), and 1 Hz curves with segments.
Model download manager: pinned HF revisions, SHA-256 checks, lazy download (RMVPE 362 MB, quality-profile models), and a licence manifest flagging NC models.
Viewer section for the report: piano roll per stem, instrument lanes, vocal contour plus keyboard range bar, drum raster. Could reuse viz canvas code.
risks: Licensing: the HT-Demucs weights have no explicit licence (Défossez, 2026-10: unclear, 6s likely CC-BY-NC). BS-Roformer-SW and Mel-RoFormer Kim are CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0. MuScriptor is CC-BY-NC and gated. ADTOF is CC BY-NC-SA and its PyTorch port has no licence file. Fine for personal use, but anything commercial needs review, and the manifest must record each model's licence.

Third-party ONNX mirrors (StemSplitio for demucs-onnx, Ryan5453 for unblend) could vanish or change; the BS-Roformer-SW host account was already deleted once in 2026. Pin revisions and SHA-256 and keep a fallback to demucs 4.1.0 on PyTorch.

DirectML is 'legacy': onnxruntime-directml 1.24.4 lags onnxruntime 1.31. Graphs with in-graph STFT fail on DML on this GPU (verified: demucs-onnx iSTFT ConvTranspose OOM, CED Reshape error). GPU use therefore needs graphs with STFT outside, plus our own host code.

Package conflict: onnxruntime and onnxruntime-directml install the same module, and demucs-onnx, swift-f0, rmvpe-onnx and audio-separator[cpu] all depend on 'onnxruntime'. Requires a uv override, and a careless 'pip install' later will silently replace the DML build.

basic-pitch 0.4.0 cannot be installed as published on Python 3.12 Windows (TensorFlow pin). It works only with the overrides, plus resampy>=0.4.3 for setuptools 84. Upstream has had no release since 2024-08, so be ready to vendor it.
libsndfile/soundfile fails on Versatile.flac ('flac decoder lost sync'); ffmpeg decodes it with one logged error. All inputs must go through ffmpeg.

htdemucs_6s guitar and piano stems bleed heavily on electronic music: on MEGAFAUNA the 'guitar' stem was active 37% of the time, which is synths. Instrument labels must be fused with the tagger and not taken from stem names.
Instrumental songs: both test tracks have essentially no lead vocal (vocal stem 50-62 dB below the mix, 0-5% voiced). Without a presence gate, the range would come from bleed and vocal chops.
Monophonic pitch trackers fail on harmonies and doubled or backing vocals, and octave errors skew the extremes. Report percentiles, not raw min/max, and add a confidence field.
AudioSet tags are coarse and poorly calibrated for instruments in dense mixes (instrument probabilities about 0.02-0.08 on the mix), and weak on synth sub-types. CLAP is the remedy if needed.
The quality profile (RoFormer on CPU via audio-separator) may exceed the 5-minute budget. Overlap was raised to 4-8 in 0.47; this was not measured.

The ROCm-on-Windows torch stack is a preview: about 1.7 GB of wheels, tied to Adrenalin 26.x and Windows 11 25H2, needs Smart App Control off, has no PEP 658 metadata, and may compile kernels on first run.
Disk: WAV stems are about 220 MB per 3.6-min song (6 stems); FLAC is about 63 MB. A long album session adds up, so make stem retention configurable.
open_questions: Is the harness personal-use only, or could output ever be commercial? This decides whether NC models (6-stem RoFormer, DrumSep, ADTOF, MuScriptor) can be defaults.

Does unblend's bs_roformer_sw_fp16.onnx (351 MB, STFT outside the graph) run on DirectML on the RX 9070, and at what speed? It needs a one-off test. If it runs in about 30 s it should replace htdemucs_6s as the default 6-stem model.
Is the ROCm torch 2.11.0+rocm7.13.0 install (about 1.7 GB) worth benchmarking for audio-separator RoFormer, DrumSep and ADTOF, or does the torch-free stack suffice?
Default 4 stems (htdemucs or htdemucs_ft quality) or 6 stems (htdemucs_6s, noisier guitar and piano)? Do the video agents actually want guitar and piano stems?
Stem format: FLAC (smaller; Chromium Web Audio, ffmpeg and Blender read it) or 16-bit WAV (universal)? Mono or stereo?
Should lead and backing vocals be split (a karaoke model) so that vocal range reflects only the lead?
Should drum hits be grouped into per-bar patterns using the beats/downbeats track output, and should note events be quantised to the beat grid?
Should CLAP be shared with the meaning/mood track, so that one model download serves open-vocabulary instruments and mood?

recommended_stack:
Python 3.12 venv managed with uv (resolution checked against x86_64-pc-windows-msvc). Pins: anthropic==2.6.0, httpx, rapidfuzz, pyyaml, numpy, onnxruntime==1.31.1, faster-whisper==1.2.1, ctranslate2==4.8.5, torch (CPU, shared with the separation track; resolves to 2.15.0), torchaudio==2.11.1, uroman==1.3.1.1, num2words. Optional: mutagen==1.48.1, stable-ts==2.19.1, transformers (CLAP). The external binary is the already-installed FFmpeg 9.0.2 Gyan full build, which has chromaprint, whisper and Vulkan.

STEP 1 - IDENTITY (<5 s).
- Run ffprobe -show_format -show_streams -of json and normalise tag keys case-insensitively: title, artist, album, album_artist, date/year, isrc, track, genre, lyrics/unsyncedlyrics/USLT, and musicbrainz_*. Record duration, sample rate and channels.
- If title or artist is missing, or --verify-identity is set: fingerprint with ffmpeg -t 120 -i IN -ac 2 -f chromaprint -fp_format base64, then POST a gzip-compressed request to api.acoustid.org/v2/lookup (client=ACOUSTID_API_KEY env, duration = full integer seconds, meta=recordings+releasegroups+compress; at most 3 req/s).
- Then GET musicbrainz.org/ws/2/recording/{mbid}?inc=artist-credits+releases+work-rels+artist-rels+url-rels+tags+genres+isrcs (1 req/s, User-Agent 'mv-harness/<ver> ( contact )').
- With tags but no MBID: run a MusicBrainz search by recording+artist and an ISRC lookup, and accept a match only if its score is at least 90 and the length is within ±3 s.
- Cache every response under out/<song>/cache/.

STEP 2 - LYRICS ACQUISITION (priority order, first hit wins; record which source was used).
(a) User file via --lyrics: .lrc (including [offset:], multiple timestamps per line, and A2 <mm:ss.xx> word tags), .srt/.vtt, LRCLIB Lyricsfile .yaml, or .txt.
(b) Embedded tag lyrics (ffprobe; mutagen for ID3 SYLT).
(c) LRCLIB with User-Agent 'mv-harness vX (url)', requests sequential and 200-500 ms apart, honoring Retry-After on 429/503:
  - GET /api/get?track_name&artist_name&album_name&duration=round(dur).
  - On 404, the same without album.
  - Then GET /api/search?track_name&artist_name (and /api/v2/search for flags). Rank results by rapidfuzz title score ≥ 90, artist score ≥ 85 and |duration diff| ≤ 2 s (accept up to ±5 s only with a 'version_mismatch' flag), then GET /api/get/{id}.
  - Prefer lyricsfile lines[].words when hasWordSync, then syncedLyrics, then plainLyrics. instrumental=true means there are no lyrics.
(d) Otherwise, transcribe (Step 4).
Store lyrics only in the local output folder and never upload them.

STEP 3 - VOCAL STEM AND VOCAL ACTIVITY.
- Take vocals.wav from the separation track and resample with ffmpeg to 16 kHz mono float32.
- Compute a vocal-activity mask by porting viz/js/audio.js envelope logic to the stem's RMS in dB: fast 8 ms and slow 90 ms envelopes, -46 dBFS gate, 4 dB re-arm. Add Silero VAD (bundled with faster-whisper) at threshold ~0.3. Silero on the full mix keeps 0 s (verified), so it must run on the stem.

STEP 4 - TRANSCRIPTION (only when there is no lyric text, or for --verify-lyrics).
- Run faster-whisper 1.2.1, WhisperModel('large-v3-turbo', device='cpu', compute_type='int8', cpu_threads=8..16), on the numpy stem decoded by ffmpeg (PyAV 19 breaks faster-whisper's own decoder).
- Settings: vad_filter=True, word_timestamps=True, condition_on_previous_text=False, beam_size=5, temperature=[0,0.2,0.4], compression_ratio_threshold=2.4, log_prob_threshold=-1.0, no_speech_threshold=0.6, hallucination_silence_threshold=2.0. Set language from tags, MusicBrainz or LRCLIB metadata when known; otherwise vote over the 3 most vocal 30 s windows.
- Post-filter:
  - drop non-lyric tags such as '(upbeat music)', '[MUSIC]', '*outro music*', '♪' and subtitle credits (all seen in tests);
  - drop n-gram loops (top trigram repeated 3 or more times, or unique-word ratio < 0.4);
  - drop segments with no_speech_prob > 0.6 and avg_logprob < -1;
  - drop words outside the vocal mask;
  - flag lines faster than 8 words/s.
- GPU fast path or fallback: ffmpeg -i vocals.wav -af "whisper=model=ggml-large-v3-turbo-q8_0.bin:vad_model=ggml-silero-v5.1.2.bin:use_gpu=1:language=xx:queue=20:max_len=1:format=json:destination=words.jsonl" -f null - (Vulkan on the RX 9070, verified).
- Opt-in --quality max uses large-v3.

STEP 5 - WORD-LEVEL FORCED ALIGNMENT (always, whatever the text source).
- Use torchaudio.pipelines.MMS_FA with get_model(with_star=True), the CPU model, on the 16 kHz vocal stem. Compute emissions in 30 s windows with 2 s context.
- Normalise text: lowercase, expand numbers with num2words, strip punctuation, romanize non-Latin scripts with uroman, and mark parenthetical backing vocals as optional.
- Align line by line inside windows built from the source line timings (LRCLIB, user LRC or Whisper) padded ±1.5 s. Without line timings, align globally with <star> between lines.
- Use torchaudio.functional.forced_align and merge_tokens to get word spans and token scores.
- Expand repeated sections when the supplied text is shorter than what is sung. MEGAFAUNA's tag has only 14 lines for 217 s, so do a quick ASR pass and match its lines to the supplied lines with rapidfuzz to place repeats.
- Estimate a global offset between source line times and aligned times; a large offset means a different master.
- Fallback when CTC coverage < 0.6: stable-ts 2.19.1 model.align(stem, text, original_split=True) on a faster-whisper model. Keep a vendored numpy/numba CTC Viterbi (~60 lines, modelled on ctc-forced-aligner's C++) in case a future torchaudio drops forced_align.

STEP 6 - CONFIDENCE.
- Per word: align_p = exp(mean token log-prob); asr_p = Whisper probability (if any); agree = |CTC - source/Whisper start| < 0.3 s; energy = vocal-stem RMS inside the word span relative to song vocal median; flags = zero_len, too_long, outside_vocal_mask, low_energy, interpolated.
- conf = clip(0.5*align_p + 0.25*(asr_p or align_p) + 0.15*agree + 0.10*energy_ok, 0, 1).
- Per line: mean and min of word conf, coverage = share of words with conf ≥ 0.5, timing_source, offset_ms.
- Per song: lyrics_source, lyrics_match_score (ASR vs supplied text similarity; catches wrong lyrics), alignment_coverage, and quality grade A-D.

STEP 7 - AUDIO MOOD (~1.3 s).
- onnxruntime CPU with Essentia ONNX models: msd-musicnn-1 to emomusic-msd-musicnn-2 and deam-msd-musicnn-2 for valence/arousal per 1.49 s; discogs-effnet-bsdynamic-1 to mtg_jamendo_moodtheme-discogs-effnet-1 for 56 tags per 0.99 s.
- Front end: a numpy mel port (16 kHz, 512/256, 96 slaney mel bands, log10(1+10000x), patches 187/93 and 128/62).
- Aggregate per section using the structure track.

STEP 8 - MEANING (LLM).
- Build meaning/input.json: identity and credits; external context with source URLs (MusicBrainz work/credits/tags; Wikipedia summary only through MusicBrainz or Wikidata links; Genius off by default); lyrics lines with ids L001..., start/end, section ids and repeat groups; per-section summaries from the other tracks (tempo/beat density, loudness and quiet/loud parts, instruments present, vocal range and median pitch, mood curves); and the user's notes.
- Call client.messages.parse(model='claude-opus-5-5', thinking={'type':'adaptive'}, output_config={'effort':'high','format':<schema>}, max_tokens≈16000) with server-side fallbacks enabled.
- Validate after the call: every evidence line id and time range must exist; quotes are at most 10 words and at most one per claim (references by line id are preferred); claims are typed lyric-grounded, audio-grounded, external (with URL) or speculative.
- Write meaning.json and a human-readable meaning.md. Cache by a hash of input plus schema.
- With no credentials: write prompt.md, input.json, schema.json and meaning.json {status:'pending_llm'}, plus offline heuristics (hook/repeat clusters, top content words, audio mood summary), so the agent can run the prompt itself and validate the result with 'mv-harness meaning --validate'.

STEP 9 - EXPORTS.
- lyrics.json (lines and words, with confidence), lyrics.lrc (A2 enhanced word tags), lyrics.srt/.vtt, karaoke .ass (\k tags) for ffmpeg burn-in, and a Lyricsfile .yaml.

Expected total for a 4-min song on this PC, excluding separation:
- known lyrics: ~20-50 s (alignment dominates) + LLM 30-120 s;
- transcription path: +60-150 s on CPU, or +15-40 s on the ffmpeg Vulkan path.

custom_code_needed: LRC/A2/SRT/VTT/TXT/Lyricsfile parser and writer: [offset:] tags, multiple timestamps per line, A2 <mm:ss.xx> word tags, parenthetical backing-vocal detection, line normalisation. pylrc is stale (2020, sdist only), so write ~150 lines ourselves.

LRCLIB client: matching cascade (get with album, then without album, then search plus fuzzy ranking with rapidfuzz, then get/{id}); ±2 s duration rule with a 'version_mismatch' flag; Lyricsfile YAML parsing (lines[].text/start_ms/end_ms, words[].text/start_ms, metadata.language/instrumental); User-Agent; sequential 200-500 ms pacing; Retry-After with jitter; on-disk cache. Never call /api/get-cached; never publish unless the user explicitly opts in.

Identity resolver: ffprobe tag normalisation across Vorbis/ID3/MP4 keys; chromaprint via the ffmpeg muxer; gzip POST to AcoustID; MusicBrainz client with a 1 req/s limiter; score and length gates; credits extraction.

Vocal activity detector: port viz/js/audio.js's dB envelope logic (fast 8 ms / slow 90 ms envelopes, -46 dBFS gate, 4 dB dip re-arm) and apply it to the vocal-stem RMS. Combine with Silero VAD. Used to reject words in silence and to compute per-word vocal energy.

CTC alignment wrapper around torchaudio MMS_FA: windowed emissions (30 s windows, 2 s context), <star> insertion, line-window-constrained alignment, uroman romanisation, num2words, repeated-section expansion (match ASR lines to supplied lines when the text is shorter than the singing), global offset estimation. Plus a vendored numpy/numba Viterbi fallback (~60 lines, modelled on ctc-forced-aligner's 97-line C++) in case torchaudio drops forced_align.

Whisper hallucination filter: non-lyric tag blacklist ('(upbeat music)', '[MUSIC]', '*outro music*', '♪', subtitle credits), n-gram loop detector, no_speech/avg_logprob/compression-ratio rules, words-per-second sanity check, vocal-mask gating. Also language voting over the most vocal windows.
faster-whisper input shim: decode audio with ffmpeg to 16 kHz float32 numpy, because faster-whisper 1.2.1's own decoder crashes with PyAV 19.0.2 (verified).

Confidence model: per-word conf from align_p, asr_p, timing agreement and vocal energy; line and song aggregates; lyrics_match_score (ASR vs supplied text) to detect wrong or partial lyrics; quality grade.

Essentia front-end port in numpy: 16 kHz, 512/256 hann, power spectrum, 96 slaney mel bands with slaney normalisation, log10(1+10000x), patches 187/93 (musicnn) and 128/62 (effnet). Plus ONNX runners and per-section aggregation. Validate against reference Essentia outputs once on Linux CI if possible.

Meaning pass: input builder that compresses the other tracks into per-section summaries (loud/quiet parts, instruments, vocal range, beat density, mood curves); JSON schema; Claude call (structured output, adaptive thinking, effort high, refusal and fallback handling); validator (citation ids and time ranges resolve, quote-length cap, claim typing); meaning.md renderer; input-hash cache; no-key prompt-bundle writer and a '--validate' command for agent-produced meaning.json; offline heuristics (repeat/hook clusters, top content words) for when no LLM runs or the song is instrumental.
Exporters: enhanced LRC, SRT/VTT, ASS karaoke with \k timing for ffmpeg subtitles burn-in, per-word JSON for Remotion/WebGL.
risks: Whisper on the full mix is unusable (verified on this machine). The ggml base model emitted only '(upbeat music)', '[MUSIC]' and '*outro music*' for Versatile. faster-whisper small detected Russian (p=0.37) for English MEGAFAUNA and recalled 0% of the known lyric word sequence; base recalled 24%. Silero VAD on the full mix kept 0 s. Transcription and VAD must therefore run on the separated vocal stem, which makes this track depend on separation quality.

faster-whisper 1.2.1 (last release Oct 2025) breaks with the current PyAV 19.0.2 when given a file path (TypeError: unexpected keyword 'metadata_errors'; verified). Always pass ffmpeg-decoded numpy arrays, or pin av to an older version. The project's release pace has slowed.

Licensing: MMS_FA / mms-300m weights are CC-BY-NC 4.0, Essentia models are CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, ctc-forced-aligner is CC-BY-NC, the AcoustID service is non-commercial, and mutagen is GPL. That is fine for personal use, but it blocks commercial use or redistribution of outputs from those models without replacements.

torchaudio is in maintenance mode. Its docs say the forced-alignment APIs were removed in 2.9, yet the 2.11.1 Windows wheel still ships forced_align and MMS_FA with no deprecation in code (verified by inspecting the wheel). Pin torchaudio and keep a vendored Viterbi fallback. The torch 2.15 + torchaudio 2.11.1 combination resolves but was not imported at runtime (torch not installed, per the rules).

LRCLIB coverage of niche tracks is low: neither test song is present. Search returns false friends: q='Versatile' surfaces a different song by the artist 'Versatile' at 225 s vs our 228 s, so require artist similarity. Line timings may come from a different master or edit, so global offset detection is needed. Word sync is rare (~3% of sampled records), and the syncedLyrics field never contained A2 word tags (0 of 160).

Embedded or user lyrics can be partial: MEGAFAUNA's tag has 14 lines for a 217 s song, probably one pass with repeats unsung in the text. Global CTC alignment of shortened text will mis-place words, so repeat expansion driven by a quick ASR pass is needed.

LRCLIB etiquette and limits: ~90 req/min per IP for identified clients; 429/503 with Retry-After; ignoring them risks a temporary ban. /api/get-cached returned 404 even for a known record and is undocumented, so do not rely on it.

The ffmpeg whisper filter exists only in FFmpeg builds with --enable-whisper (the installed Gyan full build has it; other builds may not). It provides no token probabilities, and its fixed queue windows split words at boundaries (a duplicated word was observed). Model files (ggml) must be downloaded and managed separately.

Speed estimates for large-v3-turbo are extrapolated from base/small measurements, not measured: CPU int8 ~60-150 s per 4-min stem, Vulkan ~15-40 s. If separation plus transcription exceeds the ~5 min budget, switch the default transcriber to the ffmpeg Vulkan path.

AMD GPU paths on Windows are fragile: CTranslate2 has no ROCm on Windows; torch-directml is stale (torch 2.4.1); DirectML is in sustained engineering (Windows ML is the successor, and AMD MIGraphX EP general availability is planned for 2026); ROCm PyTorch for Windows comes from AMD's index, not PyPI, and has no Triton. The design keeps every step CPU-viable.

The Essentia mel front-end is a numpy re-implementation, not bit-exact. Valence from the emoMusic and DEAM heads disagrees (MEGAFAUNA 3.6 vs 6.1), so present audio valence as low-confidence and favour arousal.

LLM meaning can invent facts about obscure artists: there is no Wikipedia page for Kitcaliber, and MusicBrainz has only credits and 'virtual band'/'furry' tags. Mitigate by typing every claim (lyric-grounded, audio-grounded, external with URL, or speculative) and validating citations. Instrumentals or songs with very little text get an explicitly speculative, audio-led interpretation.

Copyright: lyric text, and any Genius annotations, must stay in the user's local output folder and never be sent anywhere except the configured LLM call. meaning.json should reference lines by id with very short quotes at most. The harness must never publish to LRCLIB unless the user explicitly opts in.
open_questions: Are non-commercial model licences (MMS_FA CC-BY-NC, Essentia CC BY-NC-ND, AcoustID non-commercial) acceptable, given this is a personal tool? If not, we need replacements: wav2vec2 Apache-2.0 per-language aligners, and our own mood model.
Will the user register a free AcoustID application key (needed only for untagged files), and optionally an LRCLIB app id for higher rate limits?

Default transcriber: run a benchmark of faster-whisper large-v3-turbo int8 CPU vs the ffmpeg whisper filter with ggml-large-v3-turbo on the RX 9070 (Vulkan), on the real vocal stems, before choosing. That needs ~1.5 GB plus ~0.6-0.8 GB of model downloads, which were skipped in this research.
Should the meaning pass run by default (costs ~$0.10-0.40 per song on claude-opus-5-5 with an API key), or only on request, with the prompt bundle as the default output?
Should non-English lyrics get a translation and gloss inside the meaning pass (Versatile's language is unknown until transcription; Cosmic may not be English)?
How should user-supplied external context be provided (artist statement, liner notes, interview links)? A --notes file fed into meaning/input.json is proposed.
Should Genius context be supported at all (token required; annotations copyrighted), or only Wikipedia and MusicBrainz?

Is the full LRCLIB Lyricsfile spec published anywhere other than the JS-only lrclib.net/lyricsfile page? Are there optional fields such as singer/agent or word end_ms beyond what the samples showed (lines[].text/start_ms/end_ms, words[].text/start_ms, metadata.language/instrumental)?
Runtime check still needed: import torch 2.15 CPU + torchaudio 2.11.1 on Windows and run MMS_FA forced_align end to end on a stem (not done, to avoid the torch download during research).
Does the user want the harness to optionally contribute verified word-synced lyrics back to LRCLIB (publish requires a proof-of-work token)? The recommendation is no by default.

track: Prior art and the agent-facing output contract (manifest, song brief, curves, events, helpers, CLI, skill/MCP wrapper, verification viewer)

candidates.name: Spotify Web API Audio Analysis and Audio Features schema (reference only)
candidates.provides: Reference schema. Track scalars: tempo, time_signature, key and mode (each with a confidence), loudness, end_of_fade_in and start_of_fade_out. Interval lists: bars, beats and tatums (start, duration, confidence). Sections: start, duration, loudness, tempo, key, mode, time_signature, all with confidences. Segments: loudness_start, loudness_max, loudness_max_time, loudness_end, 12-value chroma (pitches) and 12-value timbre. Audio Features adds danceability, energy, valence and others.
candidates.windows_install: not applicable (web API). Since 2024-11-27, apps created after that date get 403 from audio-features and audio-analysis.
candidates.license: proprietary API, closed to new apps
candidates.reason: Adopt as the conceptual template, not as a dependency. Worth copying: (1) a confidence on every estimate; (2) several time granularities (tatum, beat, bar, section) on one second-based timeline; (3) the segment attack summary (loudness_start, loudness_max, loudness_max_time), a compact way to describe each hit for visuals; (4) fade-in end and fade-out start as scalars. Avoid: opaque timbre vectors with no meaning attached, and black-box 'valence' or 'danceability' numbers with no provenance.
candidates.quality_notes: The docs contradict themselves on the length of pitches and timbre (12 in the text, 3 in the example). Nothing open replaces the API; the alternatives are scrapers or paid services.

candidates.name: mvh custom contract: JSON manifest plus JSON Schema 2020-12, raw little-endian binary curves, JSON event lists, MIDI, LRC/WebVTT, brief.md, viewer.html
candidates.provides: The whole agent-facing output: an index manifest, dense curves at a fixed 100 Hz rate, event lists in seconds, notes as MIDI plus JSON, lyrics, meaning, stems, a token-bounded song brief and a verification viewer
candidates.windows_install: verified-resolves: the core needs only numpy 2.5.4, jsonschema 4.26.0, mido 1.3.3 and soundfile 0.14.0 (uv pip compile for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, py3.12: 33 packages, all wheels). Prototype run natively on this machine.
candidates.speed_estimate: Contract layer under 2 s for a 4-minute song. Prototype on MEGAFAUNA.flac (217 s): ffmpeg decode 0.09 s, 9 curves at 100 Hz with numpy 0.68 s, 782 KB of f32. Python and Node samplers agree to within 5.6e-7 at 24, 30 and 60 fps.
candidates.reason: No existing format covers fps-agnostic dense curves, events, stems, notes, lyrics, an interpretive meaning layer and an LLM-sized summary together. Pattern: the glTF idea of a small JSON index with accessors into raw binary buffers, plus Vamp-style sampleType descriptors (fixed-rate curve versus variable-rate events). Every consumer stack can read it: JS Float32Array, numpy.fromfile, Blender's bundled numpy, ComfyUI, Remotion (staticFile plus fetch), and WebGL textures.
candidates.quality_notes: Prototype at C:\Users\OPENSR~1\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\18e41bb73b27f8e3\cfc48f00-d046-409f-8e46-ef42c153038f\scratchpad\research\prior-art-contract\proto\ (proto_write.py, mvh_sample.py, mvh_sample.mjs).

candidates.name: JAMS (JSON Annotated Music Specification)
candidates.provides: A JSON container of annotations; each observation is {time, duration, value, confidence} under a namespace (beat, beat_position, segment_open, key_mode, tempo, chord, note_midi, pitch_contour, lyrics, mood_thayer, tag_open and others), with per-annotation annotation_metadata and a mir_eval bridge
candidates.windows_install: wheels-on-pypi: jams-0.3.5-py3-none-any.whl. Resolves on Windows but pulls pandas 3.1.1, scipy 1.18.1, mir-eval 0.8.2 and others (16 packages).
candidates.reason: Not the primary contract. JSON-only dense data (pitch_contour, curves) is bloated and slow to parse, and the format has no notion of stems, files, fps or a summary. The library is heavy for what it adds and releases are slow. Borrow its observation shape, its namespace names as the 'kind' vocabulary for events, and its annotation_metadata idea. Offer 'mvh export --jams' later if MIR evaluation is ever needed.

candidates.name: All-In-One Music Structure Analyzer (allin1)
candidates.provides: Per-track JSON with path, bpm, beats[], downbeats[], beat_positions[] (1..N), and segments [{start, end, label}] using the Harmonix labels (intro, verse, chorus, bridge, inst, outro, start, end). Optional frame activations and embeddings, a PNG visualisation, and sonification (click track).
candidates.windows_install: sdist-needs-compiler in practice. The allin1 wheel is pure Python, but Windows also needs NATTEN built from source, madmom from git (needs a C compiler) and torch (CUDA by default).
candidates.reason: Not adopted as a dependency for this track; the analysis tracks decide on structure models. Copy: its simple, flat beats/downbeats/beat_positions/segments JSON (our events mirror it), and its '--sonify' idea, which becomes the viewer's metronome click for checking beats by ear. Avoid: one monolithic JSON per track with no units, schema version or provenance.

candidates.name: beatlyzer
candidates.provides: An 'LLM-friendly' JSON under schema id 'beatlyzer.analysis/v1' (metadata, loudness, brightness, sections, events: beat_drop / volume_surge / high_tone with descriptions, energy_profile, summary_text, ai_notes), a 4-panel PNG, a Markdown report, and a stdio MCP server (analyze_audio)
candidates.windows_install: git-only install of a pure-Python librosa stack; probably resolves on Windows, not tested
candidates.last_release: no PyPI release; repo last pushed 2026-07-07 (2 stars)
candidates.reason: Too new and small to depend on, with shallow librosa heuristics. Copy: a schema id string in every file; a self-describing 'ai_notes' field that explains units; events that carry a one-line description for LLMs; and the paired machine JSON plus human Markdown report. Avoid: 'm:ss' strings as the primary time unit (we use float seconds and only render m:ss in the brief), and mixing the dense energy profile into the summary JSON.

candidates.name: audio-analyzer-rs (Rust MCP server)
candidates.provides: MCP tools audio_info, spectral_features, harmonic_analysis, rhythm_analysis, full_analysis and compare. Outputs compact text: 7 producer bands, EBU R128 LUFS/LRA/true peak, HPSS percussive ratio, stereo field and section boundaries. Downsampled time series on request via start_time/end_time and a resolution.
candidates.windows_install: prebuilt Windows binaries (audio-analyzer-win32-x64.mcpb and an mcp-server binary) on GitHub Releases; pure Rust, no Python or ffmpeg
candidates.speed_estimate: Author's claim: about 2 s for a 60 s track including separation
candidates.reason: Best prior art for token-efficient agent design: a 'summary then zoom' workflow, under 1% of context per analysis. Our MCP and skill copy it: get_brief first, then get_window(t0, t1, curves, rate). Usable as an independent cross-check of LUFS and key during QA. Not a substitute, because it returns text rather than files at fixed rates.

candidates.name: mcp-local-music-analysis and hugohow/mcp-music-analysis
candidates.provides: librosa wrappers that return tempo, beats, key, MFCC means and stds, and spectral stats in one call (hugohow adds Whisper and YouTube or URL input)
candidates.windows_install: wheels-on-pypi (mcp-local-music-analysis 0.1.0, 2026-05-23); hugohow is installed from git or uvx
candidates.reason: Shallow: global statistics only, no time-resolved contract, no stems or notes. Shows that 'MCP returns a JSON blob' is the common baseline we need to beat.

candidates.name: AutoMV (multi-agent music video system, arXiv 2512.12196)
candidates.provides: The closest prior art to an agent music-video harness. A preprocessing stage (SongFormer structure and beats, htdemucs vocals, Whisper lyrics with timestamps, Qwen2.5-Omni captions for genre, mood and vocalist) feeds Screenwriter, Director and Verifier agents and a character bank.
candidates.windows_install: linux-only in practice (conda, CUDA, cloud API keys for Gemini, Doubao, Aliyun and others)
candidates.reason: Not a dependency. It validates our split: deterministic MIR preprocessing, then text artefacts for agents. Copy: natural-language music captioning (genre, mood, vocalist attributes) next to the numbers, and the idea of a verifier step. Avoid: an internal, undocumented hand-off between stages. Ours is a versioned, public contract.

candidates.name: Parseq (Deforum parameter sequencer)
candidates.provides: Keyframes with expression-based interpolation: frame/beat/second units (f, b, s), conversion functions (f2b, b2f, s2f), beat-synced oscillators (sin, sq, tri, saw, pulse, with p=4b), audio event to keyframe generation, and an amplitude and pitch timeseries import
candidates.windows_install: not applicable (browser app)
candidates.reason: Copy the helper vocabulary into mvh.js and mvh_load.py: beat position b(t), beat and bar phase, unit conversion, and oscillators locked to the beat grid. These let agents write 'pulse every 2 beats' without re-deriving the grid. Don't depend on it.

candidates.name: Deforum keyframe schedule strings
candidates.provides: Strings of the form '0:(v0), 1:(v1), ...', indexed by frame
candidates.windows_install: not applicable (text format)
candidates.reason: A cheap export adapter (mvh frames --format deforum --curve bands.bass --fps 15). Known pitfall: values that fall on the same frame overwrite each other, so aggregate per frame first (our mean or max resample policy).

candidates.name: ComfyUI_Yvann-Nodes (audio reactivity)
candidates.provides: Inside ComfyUI: stem-based (drums, vocals, bass) per-frame weight lists, peak indices to switch IPAdapter images, and audio prompt schedules
candidates.windows_install: installed through ComfyUI-Manager (runs inside ComfyUI)
candidates.reason: A consumer, not a dependency (and GPL). It shows that ComfyUI pipelines want per-frame float lists at the video fps and peak frame indices. So mvh frames must export fps-resampled CSV/JSON, and events must be convertible to frame indices with a documented rounding rule.

candidates.name: ComfyUI_RyanOnTheInside (Flex Features)
candidates.provides: Per-frame 'features' from audio (amplitude envelope, RMS, centroid, onsets, chroma), from MIDI files (velocity, pitch, note on/off, duration, density, pitch bend, CC) and from Whisper text (word timing, sentiment)
candidates.windows_install: installed through ComfyUI-Manager
candidates.reason: A consumer. It confirms that a Standard MIDI File of transcribed notes is directly usable downstream, so emit notes/notes.mid with one track per source alongside notes.json. Word-level lyric timings are also a first-class driver.

candidates.name: Neural Frames (commercial audio modulation)
candidates.provides: Automatic 8-stem split (kick, snare, hihats, toms, drums, bass, vocals, other) and DAW-automation-like modulation: an audio stem envelope times an amplitude, added to a target such as zoom, strength or rotation, plus tempo-synced oscillators
candidates.windows_install: not applicable (SaaS)
candidates.reason: Copy the insight that drum sub-stems (kick, snare, hats) are the most useful visual drivers. Our contract carries per-drum hit events and envelopes (from drum transcription or a drum sub-split), not only bass/mid/high.

candidates.name: Remotion @remotion/media-utils (visualizeAudio, useWindowedAudioData)
candidates.provides: An FFT spectrum per frame (numberOfSamples bins), computed at render time from decoded audio, plus waveform helpers. No precomputed beats, onsets or sections.
candidates.license: Remotion License (free for individuals and small teams; companies need a licence)
candidates.reason: Not an analysis source, but a key consumer. Our JS helper must be synchronous and pure once loaded (load in calculateMetadata or delayRender, then sample by frame/fps) so Remotion's parallel, out-of-order frame rendering stays deterministic. Our curves replace the raw-FFT bars with musically meaningful drivers.

candidates.name: Sonic Visualiser 5.x / Vamp plugin outputs
candidates.provides: Annotation layers (time instants, time-value, regions, notes) that import and export as CSV (time, value, duration, label). Vamp output descriptors: sampleType OneSamplePerStep / FixedSampleRate / VariableSampleRate, hasDuration, binCount, binNames, unit.
candidates.windows_install: official Windows installer
candidates.reason: Copy the descriptor model. Every mvh track declares kind (curve at a fixed rate, or events at variable times), whether it has durations, channel names and units. Optional 'mvh export --sv-csv' lets a human load our beats or notes over the spectrogram in Sonic Visualiser as a second QA view.

candidates.name: LRC / Enhanced LRC, WebVTT, ASS lyric formats
candidates.provides: LRC: [mm:ss.xx] line timing (what lrclib's syncedLyrics returns), with optional <mm:ss.xx> word timing in Enhanced LRC. WebVTT: cue timing plus inline <hh:mm:ss.ttt> timestamps (karaoke), native browser <track> support, and ffmpeg subtitle burn-in. ASS: \k karaoke styling via libass.
candidates.windows_install: not applicable (text formats, about 50 lines of writer code)
candidates.reason: lyrics.json is canonical (lines plus words with t and d, source, offset, confidence). Also write lyrics.lrc and lyrics.vtt so ffmpeg, browser and NLE agents need no conversion. ASS is an optional extra.

candidates.name: MIDI (Standard MIDI File) via mido

recommended_stack:
CONTRACT AND INVOCATION LAYER (this track). Native Windows, Python 3.12.10 via 'python -m uv', ffmpeg 9.0.2 external.

1. Package and CLI. A uv project 'mvh' with a console script. Use stdlib argparse to keep dependencies down. Core contract deps (verified to resolve for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, all wheels): numpy==2.5.4, jsonschema==4.26.0, mido==1.3.3, soundfile==0.14.0. Optional extra [mcp]: mcp>=2.3,<3. Analysis models come from the other tracks as optional extras, so the contract layer installs in seconds. Minimal commands:
   - mvh analyze <audio> --out <dir> [--only/--skip/--force <stages>] [--lyrics file.lrc|.txt] [--no-network] [--device auto|cpu|dml] [--fps 24,30,60] [--meaning agent|ollama:<model>|anthropic|off]. Progress goes to stderr. One JSON line on stdout ({manifest, brief, viewer, warnings}) so agents can parse the result.
   - mvh status <dir> [--json]: per stage done, stale or pending, with the reason (input hash, params or version changed) and timings.
   - mvh frames <dir> --fps N [--curves a,b] [--format csv|json|deforum]: fps-resampled per-frame table for ComfyUI, Deforum, After Effects or ffmpeg.
   - mvh validate <dir>: JSON Schema check of every file, including an agent-written meaning.json.
   - mvh view <dir>: opens viewer.html; works from file://, no server needed.
   - mvh brief <dir>: re-renders brief.md, for example after the meaning stage is filled.

2. Stage graph with content-addressed cache. Stages: ingest (decode to PCM, sha256 of the decoded PCM, tags, attached cover art via ffmpeg -map 0:a:0 / -map 0:v, preview audio, lossless reference copy if the input is lossy), stems, rhythm, spectral, dynamics, structure, instruments, notes, vocals, harmony, lyrics, meaning, brief, viewer.
   - Cache key = sha256(PCM hash + stage name + stage code version + params + model weight hashes + upstream keys). Results live under <out>/.cache/<stage>/<key>/; --cache-dir can move the cache.
   - Writes are atomic (temp file, then rename). Reruns skip unchanged stages.
   - Determinism: fixed seeds; floats rounded in JSON (times to 1 ms, values to 4 significant digits); sorted keys; UTF-8 with ensure_ascii=False.
   - All volatile data (timestamps, timings, device, host) goes to run.json, never manifest.json, so reruns are byte-identical and diffable.
   - GPU (DirectML) jitter: compare with a tolerance and record the device used.

3. Output layout (each out dir is self-contained):
   - manifest.json: index only. Holds schema_version, source info, timebase, summary scalars and a files[] descriptor. Never inline arrays. Target under 3k tokens.
   - brief.md: target under 2.5k tokens, hard cap 4k.
   - viewer.html
   - schema/*.schema.json (draft 2020-12, semver; additive changes are minor versions, breaking changes are major)
   - lib/mvh.js (zero-dependency ES module for browser, Node and Remotion) and lib/mvh_load.py (numpy only; works in Blender's bundled Python and ComfyUI)
   - audio/: preview.opus for the viewer, reference.flac only when the input was lossy (MP3/AAC encoder delay shifts times by about 20-50 ms when decoders differ; all times refer to the harness decode)
   - stems/*.flac
   - curves/core.f32 (row-major [frames x channels], little-endian float32, 100 Hz, t_i = i/100) plus an optional core.csv mirror; curves/spectrum128.u8 (quantised dB with scale and offset in the descriptor; also usable directly as an R8 texture); curves/chroma.f32; curves/stems.f32; curves/vocal.f32
   - events/*.json: arrays of {t, d?, ...} in float seconds from the first sample, each file carrying name, kind (JAMS-style vocabulary), fields with units, and provenance
   - notes/notes.mid and notes/notes.json
   - lyrics/lyrics.json, lyrics/lyrics.lrc, lyrics/lyrics.vtt
   - meaning/meaning.json (plus request.md when an agent fills it)
   - tables/beats.csv and tables/bars.csv (beat- and bar-synchronous feature aggregates: the middle granularity agents reason with)
   - frames/<fps>fps.csv (on demand)
   - artwork/cover.jpg
   - run.json

4. Curve descriptor (Vamp-style). Each channel declares name (dotted id such as bands.bass), unit (0..1, dB, LUFS, Hz, midi), norm (for 0..1 curves: method p05-p99 with lo_db and hi_db, so quiet songs still drive visuals; the absolute _db twin is always present), resample policy and a description. Resample policy: linear for smooth controls, mean for levels, max for hit envelopes so transients survive 24 fps, hold for step data.
   - Frame convention: frame n at fps F has time n/F and window [n/F, (n+1)/F). This matches Remotion frame/fps, ffmpeg and ComfyUI index 0. Blender needs an offset parameter (frame_start=1).
   - Event to frame: round to the nearest frame. That is at most half a frame late, about 21 ms at 24 fps, inside ITU-R BT.1359's 45 ms limit for audio leading; an 'early' option uses floor.

5. Helpers (identical semantics in JS and Python, checked by shipped golden vectors):
   - load(dir); curve(id).at(t); sample(id, frame, fps); framesTable(fps)
   - events(name).between(t0, t1); eventsInFrame(name, n, fps)
   - pulse(events, t, {attack, decay}) for flash-on-hit envelopes
   - beatPos(t), beatPhase(t), barPhase(t) and beat-locked oscillators (Parseq-style units f, b, s)
   - section(t); lyricAt(t) giving line and word plus progress
   - noteAt(t, source); vocalAt(t)
   - toTexture(gl, id) to pack curves into a WebGL2 R32F or R8 texture
   - Prototype check: Python and Node samplers agree to within 5.6e-7 at 24, 30 and 60 fps.

6. LLM-facing summary. brief.md sections:
   - one-table header: title, artist, duration, BPM, meter, key, integrated LUFS, LRA, vocal range, instrumentation
   - 'What the song is about' (true meaning, paraphrased, with confidence and sources)
   - section cue sheet: start-end in s and m:ss.s, bars, label, energy, loudness class, active instruments, vocals and their range, notable hits, lyric line indices, mood (valence/arousal), meaning of the section
   - up to 15 top moments (drops, builds, breakdowns, silences, biggest hits, highest and lowest vocal notes, key changes) with times
   - a file index with one-line loader snippets (JS and Python)
   - warnings
   Every number in the brief is reproducible from the files.

7. Meaning stage protocol. Deterministic stages never need an API key.
   - Default --meaning agent: the harness writes meaning/request.md (structure, lyrics, audio descriptors, tags, schema) and marks the stage 'pending-agent'. The calling agent, following the skill, writes meaning.json, then runs mvh validate and mvh brief.
   - Headless alternatives: ollama:<model> (Ollama is installed locally) or anthropic (API key).
   - With no lyrics (instrumental), the meaning comes from title, tags and mood and is flagged lower confidence.

8. Agent integration.
   - Minimal: an Agent Skill folder mv-harness/ with SKILL.md (run mvh analyze; read brief.md first; never cat curves or events into context; use lib loaders; fill meaning when pending; check with mvh view), references/CONTRACT.md (field reference) and references/RECIPES.md (Remotion, three.js/WebGL, Blender, ComfyUI, ffmpeg snippets).
   - Phase 2: a thin MCP server (mcp 2.3 MCPServer, stdio) exposing analyze, status, get_brief, get_window and list_events, using the summary-then-zoom pattern from audio-analyzer-rs.

9. Verification viewer (viewer.html). One self-contained, file://-safe page, data inlined, no CDN. All lanes share one zoomable time axis and a playhead synced to audio. Click seeks; space plays and pauses; arrow keys step a beat or a frame; lanes can be toggled. Lanes:
   - (a) Overview: mix waveform tinted by bass/mid/high with section blocks and labels.
   - (b) True meaning: global panel (themes, narrative arc, imagery and motifs, confidence and sources) plus per-section meaning and mood chips that follow the playhead.
   - (c) Lyrics: line blocks with word ticks and a karaoke readout highlighting the current word.
   - (d) Beats: beat ticks, bold downbeats with bar numbers, tempo curve, and an optional WebAudio metronome click to check beats by ear.
   - (e) Hits and onsets: kick, snare and hat rows plus per-band onsets, sized by velocity.
   - (f) Bands: bass, mid and high plus the kick envelope, with an optional 128-band spectrogram heatmap.
   - (g) Loud and quiet: momentary and short-term LUFS with shaded dynamics segments (silence, quiet, medium, loud, peak), build/drop/breakdown markers and the integrated-LUFS line.
   - (h) Instruments: one activity strip per stem or instrument, with tags, and solo/mute when stem previews exist.
   - (i) Notes: a piano roll with note-name axis, coloured by source, opacity by velocity, with key and chord labels.
   - (j) Vocal range: vocal f0 contour on a note axis, a shaded tessitura band (p10-p90), markers on the lowest and highest sustained notes (click to jump), per-section range bars and a text readout such as 'A2-E5, 2.6 oct'.
   Also: a header of global facts; a readout of time in s, bar.beat and frame at a chosen fps; a 'values at this frame' panel computed with the same helper rules; and a warnings and low-confidence panel.

10. Optional exporters, later: Deforum schedule strings, JAMS, OTIO markers, Sonic Visualiser CSV layers, and an ffmpeg flash-on-beat sync-test video.
