custom_code_needed: Contract writers and JSON Schemas (draft 2020-12) for the manifest, curve descriptors, event files, lyrics, notes and meaning, plus 'mvh validate'. No library implements this contract.

A shared resampler with per-channel policies (linear, mean, max, hold), the frame convention t=n/fps with window [n/fps, (n+1)/fps), and nearest-frame event mapping. Implemented identically in lib/mvh_load.py and lib/mvh.js, with golden test vectors. The prototype already shows 5.6e-7 parity at 24, 30 and 60 fps on MEGAFAUNA.flac.

Helper APIs in both languages: load, curve.at, sample(frame, fps), framesTable, events.between, eventsInFrame, pulse(attack, decay) from events, beatPos, beatPhase, barPhase, beat-locked oscillators (Parseq-style f/b/s units), section(t), lyricAt(t), noteAt(t), vocalAt(t), toTexture(gl).

An offline port of viz/js/audio.js: the 128 log bands from 32 Hz to 16 kHz with the 2.6 dB/oct tilt, the band rule (bass 32-150, mid 150-2200, high 2200-16k), the kick envelope (fast 8 ms versus slow 90 ms dB envelope gap, typical-attack reference, 4 dB re-arm, -46 dBFS gate), and per-band spectral-flux onsets. Offline curves will then match what the user tuned in Quanta; an optional non-causal (zero-phase) mode removes the real-time lag.
Track-relative normalisation (p05-p99 of dB, clipped to 0..1) that always ships next to the absolute dB curves, with the normalisation parameters recorded in the descriptor.
Segmentation of loud and quiet parts from short-term LUFS (silence, quiet, medium, loud, peak) with hysteresis, a minimum duration and bar snapping, plus detection of builds, drops and breakdowns.

A vocal range summariser over the f0 contour: filter octave errors and blips under 150 ms; report lowest and highest sustained notes with timestamps, p2-p98 range, p10-p90 tessitura, span in semitones, register label, and per-section and per-phrase ranges.
Beat- and bar-synchronous aggregation tables (beats.csv, bars.csv).
A brief.md generator: header table, paraphrased meaning, section cue sheet, top moments, file index with loader snippets, warnings. It enforces a token cap and keeps verbatim lyrics out of the brief.

The meaning-stage protocol: request.md plus schema for agent fill-in, a pending-agent status, and re-rendering after validation. Optional Ollama and Anthropic backends; a fallback for instrumental tracks.
LRC (line and enhanced word timing) and WebVTT (inline word timestamps) writers, and a MIDI writer with one track per source and a tempo map derived from the beat grid (mido).

The stage DAG runner: content-addressed cache keyed on decoded-PCM sha256, stage version, params, model hashes and upstream keys; atomic writes; 'mvh status' with staleness reasons; volatile data only in run.json for byte-stable reruns.

The single-file viewer.html template (vanilla JS plus Canvas2D, data inlined, no CDN) with lanes for meaning, lyrics, beats (with metronome click), drum hits and onsets, bands and spectrogram, loudness with dynamics segments, instrument activity (stem solo), notes piano roll, and vocal range (f0 contour, tessitura band, extreme-note markers). Also a frame and bar.beat readout and a values-at-frame panel.

The Agent Skill folder (SKILL.md, references/CONTRACT.md, references/RECIPES.md for Remotion, three.js/WebGL, Blender, ComfyUI and ffmpeg) and, later, a thin MCP wrapper (mcp 2.3 MCPServer) with summary-then-zoom tools.
Small exporters: fps-resampled CSV/JSON frames, Deforum schedule strings; later JAMS, OTIO markers and Sonic Visualiser CSV layers.
Cover-art extraction (ffmpeg attached_pic) and a dominant palette; ingest must map 0:a:0 explicitly because the test FLACs carry a picture stream.
risks: Schema churn or over-design: too many fields before any consumer exists. Mitigation: ship a minimal v1 (manifest, brief, core curves, beats, sections, dynamics, lyrics, meaning, notes, vocal range, viewer), semver with additive-only minor versions, and consumers check the major version.
JS and Python helper drift makes visuals differ between stacks. Mitigation: golden sampling vectors in tests, and documented resample policies per channel.

Context blow-ups: agents may cat multi-MB curves or event JSON into context. Mitigation: the manifest never inlines arrays, the brief has a token cap, SKILL.md forbids reading curves and points to loaders, and the MCP get_window returns downsampled slices.

Timing offsets: lossy inputs (MP3/AAC encoder delay), lrclib lyrics from a different edit, and frame-numbering differences (Blender starts at frame 1, Remotion and ffmpeg at 0). Mitigation: all times are relative to the harness decode (a reference.flac is written for lossy input), lyric offsets are verified against vocal activity and recorded, and helpers take a frame0 offset.

The true-meaning layer is subjective and can hallucinate. Mitigation: label it as interpretation with confidence and sources, paraphrase rather than quote lyrics in the brief, flag instrumental or no-lyrics cases, and keep it in a separate agent-fillable stage so deterministic outputs stay reproducible.

Disk and memory: 6 stems as FLAC are about 150-250 MB per song, and a 128-band f32 matrix is 12 MB. Mitigation: u8 spectrum, FLAC stems, opt-in caches and 'mvh clean'. The viewer inlines only a 50 Hz preview pack.
file:// restrictions: fetch() of local JSON fails in Chromium, so viewer data must be inlined. Syncing several stem <audio> elements drifts slightly; acceptable for QA only.
MCP Python SDK v2 broke v1 imports (FastMCP was renamed MCPServer). Mitigation: pin mcp>=2.3,<3 and keep the wrapper thin over the Python API; the Skill plus CLI path does not depend on it.
GPU nondeterminism (DirectML or ROCm) and model updates change outputs. Mitigation: record device and weight hashes, round stored values, and compare with tolerances.
Prior-art tools are small, young or unmaintained (beatlyzer has 2 stars, Parseq was last pushed in 2023, allin1 in 2024, SongFormer has no PyPI package). Copy ideas, do not depend on them.
Windows path issues (non-ASCII titles, spaces, long paths). Mitigation: pathlib everywhere, UTF-8 file I/O, JSON written with ensure_ascii=False, and no shell-string command building.
open_questions: Canonical curve rate: 100 Hz (MIR standard, 10 ms hop, recommended) or 120 Hz (divides 24, 30, 60 and 120 fps exactly)?
Should per-fps frame tables (for example 24, 30, 60) be written by default, or only on demand via 'mvh frames'?

Who writes the true meaning by default: the calling agent through the skill (recommended, no API key), local Ollama (installed here), or an API key? And may the brief quote short lyric fragments, or paraphrase only?
Keep stems by default (disk cost), and is a drum sub-split (kick, snare, hats) wanted as a standard output?
Should the viewer let a human correct the analysis (nudge beats, relabel sections, fix lyric offsets) and save an overrides.json that later stages respect?
Is an MCP server wanted in v1, or is the Agent Skill plus CLI enough until a non-CLI host needs it?
Should the harness also render an ffmpeg A/V sync-test video (a flash on every beat, with audio) so consumers can check their own latency?
Batch or multi-song support (albums, DJ mixes with tempo changes) now, or later?
